spec_match.rationale: Probes the exact spec surfaces: navigator.globalPrivacyControl (Navigator + WorkerNavigator), the Sec-GPC header via a real same-origin echo route, and the /.well-known/gpc.json validation rules.

interactive.rationale: Every panel is driven by real buttons doing real reads/fetches; nothing is a static card.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Feature index blurb matches the ChromeStatus summary (setting, Sec-GPC: 1 header, navigator.globalPrivacyControl, gpc.json).

edge_cases.rationale: Covers absent surface (pre-157), header/DOM disagreement via gpcAtNavigation pinning, worker scope, and every unknown branch of the support resource.

conformance.rationale: New suite asserts property exposure/type/readonly, accessor shape, header-DOM consistency and the value-'1' ABNF; negative branches pass honestly when the header is absent.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Driven in headless Chrome 153 (desktop 1280px + mobile 360px): all controls exercised, console clean except the intentional, labelled 404 branch; full-page screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry asserts cover the DOM read, worker read, echo conformance and the five-variant matrix; fallback branches assert explicitly instead of faking success.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only, WCAG AA pairs reused from the established demo palette, buttons keep the paired bg/color override.

accessibility.rationale: Native controls with labels, aria-live outputs for async state, visible focus (checked in screenshot), 44px min button height.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: deno task responsive-check v157/global-privacy-control-in-chrome --merge: desktop ok, mobile ok (no horizontal overflow); table wrapped in overflow-x container; concept checked at 360px.

openQuestions.title: Verify the true-signal path on a 157+ build
openQuestions.detail: Chrome 153 here has no GPC surface, so only the absent/off branches were observable. On Chrome 157+ (or --enable-blink-features=GlobalPrivacyControlForce) verify the property reads true, the worker agrees, and the echo reports value "1".

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible live region async result status output
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce dynamic results via aria-live polite regions; don't spam interstitial states; keep one region per surface.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Each async result (worker read, header echo, variant fetch) lands in a single aria-live=polite output/verdict element; loading text is short-lived and only meaningful states are announced.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive form controls layout mobile overflow grid
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use flex-wrap/grid with intrinsic sizing and overflow-x wrappers for wide tabular content so narrow viewports never overflow horizontally.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Button groups use flex-wrap, key/value grids collapse to one column under 480px, and every table sits in an overflow-x:auto .table-wrap; verified at 360px with no horizontal overflow (deno task responsive-check + mobile screenshot).

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Native inputs with programmatic labels and aria-describedby for explanatory text.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The preferences center uses native checkboxes with <label for> and aria-describedby pointing at the rationale copy; locked state is a real disabled attribute plus visible badge text.

summary: Built and reviewed in one pass on headless Chrome 153 (no GPC surface): the page reports the honest unsupported state in window and worker scope, the echo route confirms no Sec-GPC header was sent, and the agreement verdict explains the gpcAtNavigation pinning. All three controls exercised; console and network clean.
